method: Occupational-composition method per Fable-5-team-lead instructions. Downloaded OPM data.opm.gov 'Federal Workforce Data' (FWD, FedScope's successor) employment microdata snapshot for May 2026 (file employment_202605_1, published 2026-06-30; https://data.opm.gov/api/v1/files/employment/2026/05/1/download), 2,025,993 employee-level rows, one row per employee (count=1 always). Schema includes an `occupational_category` column (OPM's white-collar PATCO-style split: ADMINISTRATIVE / PROFESSIONAL / CLERICAL / TECHNICAL / OTHER WHITE COLLAR / BLUE COLLAR) plus `occupational_series_code`/`occupational_series` (4-digit GS/wage-grade series) and `agency_subelement`/`agency_subelement_code` (bureau-level split within a department). For each of the 5 assigned agencies: (1) filtered to department_code (AG=USDA, DN=DOE federal HQ only via agency_subelement_code='DN00' to exclude FERC's DNFE rows per instructions, IN=DOI, TD=DOT, CM=DOC); (2) excluded all BLUE COLLAR-category rows (wage-grade trades/craft) automatically; (3) additionally hand-classified every occupational series with >=80 employees (covering 95-98% of each department's headcount) as field/frontline-operational (excluded) or desk/knowledge-work (included), using real-world knowledge of what each GS series does day-to-day -- e.g. Forestry Technician/Wildland Fire Management/Consumer Safety Inspection/Biological Science Technician/Wildlife-Fish Biology (field data collection, meat-plant line inspection, firefighting) excluded; Management-Program Analysis/IT/HR/Budget/Contracting/Accounting/attorneys/lab-based physical-science series included; Air Traffic Control/Aviation Safety/Railroad Safety/Motor Carrier Safety (screens-based but frontline safety-of-life operations, per explicit team-lead guidance on ATC) excluded; Park Ranger/Police/Guide/Correctional Officer (uniformed field/security) excluded. eligible_share = (total - blue_collar - named_field_series) / total. Corroborated the three largest exclusion buckets against public sources: USDA/Forest Service wildland fire workforce (~11,004 firefighters onboard May 2026, fs.usda.gov), FAA air traffic controllers (~11,000 CPCs + ~4,000 trainees, April 2026, faa.gov Controller Workforce Plan 2026-2028), and DOE M&O lab contractor workforce (bottom-up NNSA ~65,000 contractors [FAS] + Office of Science 10-lab complex ~30-35,000 [nationallabs.org / individual lab fact sheets], summing to ~95-100K, corroborating the stale FY2014 GAO-16-529 94,000 DOE-wide figure still carried as contractor_headcount). DOI has no Wave-3 row (not refreshed in the July 2026 headcount pass), so its total_headcount/headcount_as_of/source fields are carried forward unchanged from Wave-1 (W1-C.json) rather than a Wave-3 row per the task instructions; only ai_eligible_share/rationale/confidence are updated here using the new parquet-based method.

Excluded: BLUE COLLAR category (1,995) + named field/frontline white-collar series: Forestry Technician 0462 (11,372), Consumer Safety Inspection 1862 (5,221, FSIS meat/poultry line inspectors), Wildland Fire Management 0456 (4,500), Biological Science Technician 0404 (2,975), Agricultural Commodity Grading 1980 (1,565), Veterinary Medical Science 0701 (1,150, FSIS/APHIS field vets), Wildlife Biology 0486 (1,098), Agricultural Commodity Aid 1981 (746), Engineering Technical 0802 (699), Plant Protection Technician 0421 (683), Soil Conservation Technician 0458 (500), Rangeland Management 0454 (465), Food Inspection 1863 (388), Animal Health Technician 0704 (320), Fish Biology 0482 (220), Aircraft Operation 2181 (117, USFS aerial firefighting support). Total excluded = 34,014 of 77,478 (43.9%); eligible = 43,464 (56.1%, rounds to 0.56). Included as desk/knowledge work: 0401 Nat. Resources Mgmt/Bio Sci (4,759, permitting/planning analysts), 0301 Misc Admin (4,666), 0457 Soil Conservation (4,082, professional planning role), 1165 Loan Specialist (2,397, FSA/RD desk lending), 2210 IT (2,089), 0343 Program Analysis (1,814), and all HR/budget/contracting/accounting/attorney/lab-science series. Corroboration: Forest Service reports 11,004 wildland firefighters onboard as of May 29, 2026 (fs.usda.gov/managing-land/fire/workforce) against a combined FS+DOI federal wildland-fire workforce of ~18,700 (search-aggregated); USDA's own 0462+0456 exclusion here (15,872) comfortably covers that population plus non-fire forestry techs (trail/timber crews), consistent with 0462 legitimately including both.
rows.notes: -10% vs. 100,000 Wave-1 baseline as of this OIG-anchored figure (110,384 minus 20,306 documented attrition = 90,078 as of June 2025); one of the largest 2025 RIF/DRP impacts among civilian agencies (Forest Service lost 5,860 of 35,550, 16%; Rural Development lost 36%). Further declines were reported through late 2025 via a third-party FedScope aggregator (openfeds.org), landing near ~72,000 by Dec 2025 (medium confidence, not used here in favor of the more rigorously sourced OIG figure) -- flagged for a follow-up refresh. ai_eligible_share revised from 0.45 (Wave 1/3 judgment call) to 0.56 (Wave 4, OPM FWD parquet occupational-composition method).

rows.headcount_source_title: Energy Department extends hiring freeze, deems 43% workforce non-essential in reorganization plan (Federal News Network, Apr 2025)
rows.headcount_quote: The department has nearly 16,000 employees in total ... the agency is authorized to have a workforce of more than 17,500 positions.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Two-step calculation per team-lead direction (DOE's filed AI license bands include ~94K M&O lab contractors not in OPM data). STEP 1, federal employees only: OPM FWD May 2026 snapshot, department_code=DN, agency_subelement_code='DN00' (excludes FERC's DNFE rows, 1,343 employees, per instructions) -> 12,020 federal HQ/program employees. Excluded: BLUE COLLAR (1,142, mostly High Voltage Electrician/Electrical Power Controlling at the Power Marketing Administrations) + Nuclear Materials Courier 0084 (276, armed field security/transport, OTHER WHITE COLLAR category). Total excluded = 1,418; federal eligible = 10,602 of 12,020 = 88.2% (high confidence -- DOE HQ is overwhelmingly engineers/scientists/attorneys/analysts since the labs themselves are contractor-operated, not federal FTE). STEP 2, blend with M&O contractors: contractor_headcount=94,000 (carried from Wave 3, GAO-16-529, FY2014, stale but order-of-magnitude corroborated below). Contractor eligible share estimated by lab type, since the 94K M&O workforce spans both R&D labs (high eligible share) and weapons-production/security complex (low eligible share): ~40,000 NNSA R&D labs (LANL/LLNL/Sandia) at ~65% eligible (engineers/scientists dominant, some hands-on experimental/fabrication work) + ~25,000 NNSA production/security complex (Y-12, Pantex, Savannah River-adjacent) at ~30% eligible (nuclear materials production, industrial/craft-heavy, akin to a manufacturing plant) + ~32,000 Office of Science labs (Argonne, ORNL, Berkeley/LBNL, Brookhaven, Fermilab, PNNL, SLAC, Ames, Jefferson Lab, Princeton Plasma Physics) at ~72% eligible (user-facility R&D staff) = weighted contractor share ~58.3%, applied to the official 94,000 contractor_headcount = ~54,793 contractor-eligible. BLENDED: (10,602 + 54,793) / (12,020 + 94,000) = 65,395 / 106,020 = 61.7%, rounds to 0.62. This is markedly lower than the Wave 1/3 carried-forward 0.75 because the huge contractor denominator (88.7% of the blended population) pulls the federal-only 88% down toward the contractor blend's ~58%.
rows.notes: Essentially unchanged vs. 16,000 Wave-1 baseline for federal FTE, but GAO-26-108583 (Jun 2026) reports a 29.4% cumulative DOE workforce decline Dec 2024-Jan 2026 (second-steepest of 22 CFO Act agencies), implying RIF waves landed after this April 2025 snapshot and current federal headcount may be materially lower (~11k-14k) -- could not obtain a clean, directly-quotable current figure, so the April 2025 snapshot is retained rather than an unverified derived number. Contractor total (94,000) remains a decade-stale GAO-16-529 (FY2014) figure; a bottom-up 2025/2026 check (NNSA ~65,000 contractors per FAS 'Strengthening the National Labs' Workforce' + ~5 largest Office of Science labs alone summing to ~21-22K, extrapolated to ~30-35K across all 10 Office of Science labs) lands at ~95-100K, corroborating the order of magnitude but not a precise figure -- flagged for a dedicated follow-up to source a current DOE-wide M&O contractor total. Confidence is 'medium' overall: the federal-only 88.2% figure is high-confidence (direct parquet computation), but the contractor eligible-share (58.3%) and the resulting blend (0.62) rest on a constructed lab-type split rather than a directly sourced NNSA/Office of Science workforce-composition report.
rows.contractor_headcount_quote: in fiscal year 2014 the agency had about 13,000 federal employees and a contractor workforce of about 94,000
rows.denominator_basis_notes: DOE's filed AI license bands appear to count site/M&O contractor staff at the national labs (Livermore, Los Alamos, Oak Ridge, PNNL, etc.), not just federal FTE, per Fable-5-team-lead direction. This 94,000 figure is the most complete DOE-wide M&O contractor total found, but it is from FY2014 (GAO-16-529) -- 10+ years stale. A more current but narrower alternative is GAO-24-106861 (2024, FY2022 data): NNSA-only M&O contractors ~55,000 (excludes Office of Science labs); a 2026 web search finds a slightly higher current NNSA contractor figure (~65,000, FAS). Flagged for a dedicated follow-up to find a current DOE-wide M&O contractor total; use with caution.

rows.ai_eligible_rationale: OPM FWD May 2026 snapshot, department_code=IN, total 58,884 employees. Excluded: BLUE COLLAR category (7,528, mostly Maintenance Mechanic/Engineering Equipment Operating/Laboring) + named field/frontline white-collar series: Park Ranger 0025 (4,726), Wildland Fire Management 0456 (3,256), Biological Science Technician 0404 (1,578), Hydrologic Technician 1316 (1,240), Forestry Technician 0462 (656), Wildlife Refuge Management 0485 (391, field habitat management), Fish Biology 0482 (700), Wildlife Biology 0486 (636), Police 0083 (775), Guide 0090 (748), Criminal Investigation 1811 (538, DOI has field wildlife/land-crime investigators), Correctional Officer 0007 (136, BIA), Security Guard 0085 (170), Social Science Aid/Technician 0102 (97), Range Technician 0455 (95), Recreation Aid/Assistant 0189 (89). Total excluded = 23,359 of 58,884 (39.7%); eligible = 35,525 (60.3%, rounds to 0.60). Included as desk/knowledge work: 0401 Nat. Resources Mgmt/Bio Sci (3,565, permitting/NEPA analysts), 0301 Misc Admin (2,382), 2210 IT (1,662), 0343 Program Analysis (1,286), 1315 Hydrology (954, office-based analysis distinct from the field-measurement 1316 technicians), 0810 Civil Engineering (926), 1102 Contracting (806), 1301 General Physical Science (787, USGS/BOEM desk scientists), plus HR/budget/realty/attorney series. Corroboration: DOI planned ~5,700 federal + 900+ Tribal wildland firefighters for 2025 (doi.gov/wildlandfire/workforce), roughly matching this dataset's 0456+part of 0462 exclusion (~3,912) once accounting for seasonal timing differences between a May 2026 snapshot and peak fire-season staffing. This is a large jump from the 0.35 Wave-1 judgment call, driven mainly by discovering that Interior's professional/administrative/IT/engineering/contracting HQ-and-regional-office cohort (BOEM, BOR, BIA, USGS, OSMRE program staff) is a bigger share of total headcount than the field-visible NPS/BLM/FWS ranger and biologist corps that dominates public perception of the department.
rows.notes: DOI was not refreshed in the Wave-3 (July 2026) headcount pass -- no matching row exists in W3-fedscope-2026-07.json. total_headcount/headcount_as_of/headcount_source_url/headcount_source_title/headcount_quote are carried forward VERBATIM from Wave 1 (W1-C.json, 2024-09-30 doi.gov figure) unchanged; only ai_eligible_share/ai_eligible_rationale/confidence are updated here via the new OPM FWD parquet method. The headcount itself is stale (pre-dates the 2025 RIF/DRP wave that hit DOI, including ~1,000 NPS probationary firings per Outdoor Life, Feb 2025) and should be prioritized for a Wave-5 headcount-only refresh; confidence is 'medium' rather than 'high' because of this headcount/occupational-mix time mismatch (mix computed from a May 2026 snapshot applied to a Sept 2024 headcount), even though the occupational-composition arithmetic itself is directly parquet-derived. | Fable review 2026-07-05: headcount updated from the stale Sept-2024 70,000 to the researcher-verified May-2026 parquet count (58,884) so the share applies to the population it was computed from.

rows.headcount_source_title: CRS Report R48596, Department of Transportation Funding: FY2021-FY2025 Enacted and FY2026 Requested (July 2025), Table 2
rows.headcount_quote: The FY2026 budget request would increase DOT FTE staff by about 900, from 54,100 in FY2025 to 55,000 in FY2026.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: OPM FWD May 2026 snapshot, department_code=TD, total 52,721 employees. DOT's white-collar category split is dominated by ADMINISTRATIVE (42,843 of 52,721, 81%) because OPM classifies Air Traffic Control as an administrative-pay-plan series, not because DOT is mostly desk workers. Excluded (field/frontline-operational, screens-based but safety-of-life operations per team-lead ATC guidance): Air Traffic Control 2152 (19,714, the single largest series in the department), Aviation Safety 1825 (4,096, FAA inspectors doing on-site aircraft/airline/hangar inspections), Railroad Safety 2121 (473, FRA field track inspectors), Motor Carrier Safety 2123 (455, FMCSA roadside truck inspections), Air Traffic Assistance 2154 (176, ATC-floor support staff), Compliance Inspection and Support 1802 (small, field-inspection support), Aircraft Operation 2181 (small, FAA flight-inspection pilots), Highway Safety 2125 (171, field safety program). Plus BLUE COLLAR category (267, immaterial). Total excluded = 25,638 of 52,721 (48.6%); eligible = 27,083 (51.4%, rounds to 0.51). Included as desk/knowledge work: 2101 Transportation Specialist (6,509, HQ/regional program and grants analysts -- explicitly NOT the same as the operational 2152/1825 series), 0343 Program Analysis (2,437), 2210 IT (1,507), 0801/0810/0861/0855 engineering series (~3,900 combined, largely office-based design/systems engineering), 2186 Technical Systems Program Manager (679, NAS modernization desk work), attorneys/HR/budget/contracting. Corroboration: FAA reports ~11,000 Certified Professional Controllers deployed plus ~4,000 in the training pipeline as of April 2026 (faa.gov Air Traffic Controller Workforce Plan 2026-2028), a ~15,000 core-controller population; the fuller 2152 series exclusion here (19,714) additionally captures ATC supervisors/staff specialists/OJT instructors who work inside operational facilities, which is a defensible superset, not double-counting.
rows.notes: -1.6% vs. 55,000 Wave-1 baseline, within noise; not a material change to total_headcount. ai_eligible_share revised from 0.40 (Wave 1/3 judgment call) to 0.51 (Wave 4, OPM FWD parquet occupational-composition method) -- directionally similar (DOT is roughly half-eligible either way) but now arithmetic-backed and explicit about why: ATC dominates the headcount and is excluded, while the large Transportation Specialist desk-analyst cohort (which a naive department-level guess might undercount) pulls the eligible share up from what a 'mostly FAA operations' mental model would suggest.

rows.headcount_source_title: OpenFeds -- Dept. of Commerce (OPM FedScope, December 2025 Employment)
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: OPM FWD May 2026 snapshot, department_code=CM, total 40,829 employees. DOC's occupational mix is dominated by desk-based professional/administrative work: Patent Examining 1224 (9,342, USPTO, definitionally desk work), Misc Clerk 0303 (6,658), IT 2210 (2,691), Meteorology 1340 (2,151, NWS forecasters doing model-based forecasting, not field instrument maintenance), Program Analysis 0343 (1,682), Misc Admin 0301 (1,602), General Attorney 0905 (1,465), Statistics 1530 (1,310), General Physical Science 1301 (1,010, NIST desk/lab metrology), Economist, Trade Specialist, Design/Patent Examining/Attorney, Contracting, Accounting -- essentially all desk knowledge work. Excluded: BLUE COLLAR (592) + Fish Biology 0482 (591, NOAA Fisheries field/at-sea stock-assessment biologists), Electronics Technical 0856 (380, hands-on equipment repair), Meteorological Technician 1341 (101, NWS field instrument/radar maintenance), Engineering Technical 0802 (136). Total excluded = 1,800 of 40,829 (4.4%); eligible = 39,029 (95.6%, rounds to 0.96). This is a large jump from the 0.75 Wave-1/3 judgment call. Corroboration: NOAA (DOC's most field-heavy bureau) reports 10,932 total employees as of Dec 2025 and NOAA Fisheries specifically ~2,400-4,200 staff including ~900 at-sea fishery observers (search-aggregated, fisheries.noaa.gov) -- even generously counting all ~900 observers plus additional NOAA Corps/ship-crew/buoy-maintenance staff not captured under the 0482/1341/0856 series as field-excluded would only add a few hundred more exclusions, not materially changing the >90% eligible conclusion, because Census (large, desk statistical work), NIST (largely lab/office metrology), and USPTO (definitionally desk) collectively dwarf NOAA's field-operational headcount within the department total.
rows.notes: -15.8% vs. 50,000 Wave-1 baseline. Corroborates a March 2025 Government Executive report of a plan to cut ~20% of Commerce staff via attrition, plus ~880 NOAA probationary layoffs (Feb 2025) and a paused ~600-notice RIF (Census/PTO/MBDA) that drew a court TRO. 42,100 is ~12-16% actual reduction so far, short of the 20% target. total_headcount source is a third-party FedScope aggregator, not a direct FedScope pull (unchanged from Wave 3). Confidence on the NEW ai_eligible_share is 'medium' rather than 'high' despite the direct parquet computation, because the magnitude of the revision (0.75 -> 0.96) is large and no single public source independently states an aggregate DOC-wide eligible-workforce percentage to cross-check against; recommend a follow-up sanity pass specifically on whether NOAA Corps commissioned officers (a separate personnel system, likely NOT captured in this OPM civilian microdata at all) should be added as a small additional field-operational exclusion.
